sourceFirstFindings: Adopted Article 11.3 establishes the 180 EC Dutch general path: 60 EC required in each of the first two years, plus a third year of three 6 EC required units, a 12 EC research unit and 30 open. The separately listed forensic minor and noncredit language requirements add no mandatory credit.

The formal sequence places Principles of Criminal Law before substantive and procedural criminal law and requires both methods units before the normal research route. The official research module corroborates group empirical investigation and individual thesis and describes a limited conditional enrolment route for students still completing qualitative methods. It does not change the normal pathway.

Histories of Gender adds historical evidence and an incarceration topic. The clinical courses cover broader assessment and treatment. One interdisciplinary option meets the substantive academic standard. Neither the cybercrime nor the forensic direction has enough distinct specialist study for a second option.
